mainTopic: Learning without understanding: the רשע ערום, the עם הארץ, and the משנה's list of מבלי עולם
overview: The amud opens with the last definition of the משנה's רשע ערום: someone who read מקרא and learned משנה but never served תלמידי חכמים. אמוראים argue over what to call such a person: עם הארץ, בור, כותי, or מגוש. רב נחמן בר יצחק backs the מגוש view with a popular saying. A ברייתא then lists definitions of an עם הארץ, ending with the view that even one who learned without serving scholars is one. The גמרא explains 'שונים' in משלי and the ברייתא calling the תנאים מבלי עולם. Both refer to people who repeat הלכות or rule from their משנה without understanding. Returning to the משנה, a ברייתא lists a praying maiden, a visiting widow, and a premature baby as מבלי עולם. The גמרא limits the maiden to fake piety like יוחני בת רטיבי. It explains the premature baby either as a scholar who scorns his teachers or as one who rules before he is ready. רב's reading of a פסוק warns against both ruling too early and refusing to rule when qualified.

steps.title: The end of the explanation of a cunning wicked person
steps.stepSummary: The last of several definitions of the משנה's רשע ערום ends here: someone who read and learned but did not serve תלמידי חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: [A רשע ערום is one] who read Scripture and learned משנה, but did not serve Torah scholars.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes one of several explanations, given on the previous amud, of who the משנה means by a רשע ערום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Such a person knows the texts but never learned the reasoning behind them from a teacher. So he looks like a scholar, but he can rule wrongly. That outward show of knowledge is what makes him 'cunning'.

keyTerms.meaning: A cunning wicked person (the משנה's phrase being explained)
Read: studied the Written Torah (מקרא)
Learned: studied משנה
Serving Torah scholars, spending time with them to learn their reasoning

steps.confusionAlert: This is not someone who never learned. He did learn the texts. What he is missing is time with a teacher to understand them.

phrases.english: who read and learned
phrases.notes: This finishes the sentence just before: 'a רשע ערום is one who…'. 'Read' means Scripture, and 'learned' means משנה.

phrases.english: but did not serve Torah scholars.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁקָּרָא וְשָׁנָה וְלֹא שִׁימֵּשׁ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to this last view, a רשע ערום is someone who learned מקרא and משנה but did not serve תלמידי חכמים.

steps.title: Three opinions on what to call such a person
steps.stepSummary: An אמוראic dispute: רבי אלעזר calls him an עם הארץ, רבי שמואל בר נחמני a בור, and רבי ינאי a כותי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: about one who read and learned but did not serve Torah scholars, רבי אלעזר says he is an עם הארץ, רבי שמואל בר נחמני says he is a בור (boor), and רבי ינאי says he is like a כותי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a disagreement among אמוראים about the right label for the person just described.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each label stresses a different weakness. An עם הארץ is ignorant, and a בור is even more uncultured. A כותי keeps the written Torah but rejects the oral tradition of the חכמים, just as this person has the texts without the teachers' explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated: introduces a teaching or dispute of אמוראים
An ignorant, unlearned person
A boor, someone totally uncultured in learning
A Samaritan, who follows the written Torah but not the oral tradition

phrases.english: It was stated:
One who read and learned
but did not serve Torah scholars,
Rabbi Elazar says:
This one is an ignoramus.
Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said:
This one is a boor.
Rabbi Yannai says:
This one is a Samaritan.
phrases.notes: He means 'like a Samaritan': someone who has the written text but not the oral explanation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר: קָרָא וְשָׁנָה וְלֹא שִׁימֵּשׁ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the person defined in step 1 and asks what he should be called.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are three views of such a person: עם הארץ (רבי אלעזר), בור (רבי שמואל בר נחמני), or כותי (רבי ינאי).

steps.title: A fourth opinion: he is like a sorcerer
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says such a person is a מגוש (sorcerer).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב says: he is a מגוש (sorcerer).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a fourth opinion to the list: this person is like a מגוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מגוש recites spells and impresses people without understanding them. The comparison stresses that this person repeats words he does not understand and misleads others with them. The next step explains why this view makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: A sorcerer or magician who chants spells

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov says:
This one is a sorcerer.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: הֲרֵי זֶה מָגוֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth label to the three opinions in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Such a person is like a מגוש.

steps.title: Support for the sorcerer opinion from a popular saying
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says רב אחא בר יעקב's view is most reasonable, based on a folk saying that compares the תנא to a chanting sorcerer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It makes sense to follow רב אחא בר יעקב, because people say: 'The sorcerer chants and doesn't know what he's saying; the תנא recites and doesn't know what he's saying.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק picks one of the four opinions and backs it up with something people commonly say.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying puts the sorcerer and the reciter side by side: both say words without understanding them. That matches the person who learned משנה without a teacher. So the מגוש label fits him best.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reasonable / it makes sense
As people say: introduces a popular saying
Mutters or chants
Here, a reciter of משניות and ברייתות who memorizes them

steps.whatToRemember: Of the four labels, רב נחמן בר יצחק favors מגוש: someone who recites Torah texts without understanding them is like a sorcerer mumbling spells.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
It is reasonable to follow Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov,
as people say:

phrases.aramaic: רָטֵין מָגוֹשָׁא וְלָא יָדַע מַאי אָמַר,
phrases.english: The sorcerer chants and does not know what he is saying,

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא וְלָא יָדַע מַאי אָמַר.
phrases.english: the reciter recites and does not know what he is saying.
phrases.notes: Here תנא means a person who memorizes and recites משניות, not one of the sages of the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִסְתַּבְּרָא כְּרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב, דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 3's opinion over the three in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: רב אחא בר יעקב's view that such a person is a מגוש
steps.raayaSupportSource: A popular saying that pairs the chanting sorcerer with the reciter who does not understand what he says

steps.title: A ברייתא lists definitions of an ignorant person
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives several definitions of an עם הארץ: not saying קריאת שמע with its blessings (רבי מאיר), not wearing תפילין (חכמים), having no ציצית (בן עזאי), or not raising one's sons to learn Torah (רבי יונתן בן יוסף).
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Who is an עם הארץ? רבי מאיר: anyone who doesn't say קריאת שמע morning and evening with its blessings. חכמים: anyone who doesn't put on תפילין. בן עזאי: anyone without ציצית on his garment. רבי יונתן בן יוסף: anyone who has sons and doesn't raise them to learn Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the term עם הארץ came up, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that tries to define exactly who counts as one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These definitions measure an עם הארץ by neglect of basic מצוות, not by lack of knowledge. Each תנא points to a different basic obligation. רבי יונתן בן יוסף looks at whether a person passes Torah on to his children.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught: introduces a ברייתא
The recitation of the שמע
With its blessings (before and after)
Phylacteries
Ritual fringes

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Who is an ignoramus?
Anyone who does not recite the Shema
morning and evening with its blessings,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Rabbis say:
Anyone who does not put on tefillin.
Ben Azzai says:
Anyone who has no tzitzit on his garment.
Rabbi Yonatan ben Yosef said:
Anyone who has sons
and does not raise them to study Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵיזֶהוּ עַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי אלעזר used the term עם הארץ in step 2, so the גמרא brings a ברייתא that defines it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each תנא defines an עם הארץ by a different neglected basic obligation: קריאת שמע, תפילין, ציצית, or Torah education of one's sons.

steps.title: אחרים: even one who learned but did not serve scholars
steps.stepSummary: אחרים say that even someone who reads and learns, if he did not serve תלמידי חכמים, is an עם הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחרים say: Even someone who reads and learns but did not serve Torah scholars is an עם הארץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with the strictest view, which brings us right back to the person this whole discussion started with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'even' shows that this goes further than the earlier views. A person could keep all the basic מצוות and still be called an עם הארץ if he never learned from a teacher. This matches רבי אלעזר's opinion in step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others': a תנא quoted without his name
Even: signals a bigger or less obvious case

steps.whatToRemember: Book learning alone is not enough. Learning from תלמידי חכמים, and serving them, is part of what makes someone a real Torah scholar and not an עם הארץ.

phrases.english: Others say:
Even one who reads and learns
but did not serve Torah scholars —
this is an ignoramus.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים: אֲפִילּוּ קוֹרֵא וְשׁוֹנֶה וְלֹא שִׁימֵּשׁ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ברייתא's list with the broadest definition, which connects back to steps 1 and 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even one who learned מקרא and משנה but did not serve תלמידי חכמים is an עם הארץ.

steps.title: Reading without learning makes one a בור; learning nothing is like a beast
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. One who learned only מקרא but not משנה is a בור. One who learned neither is described by a פסוק about the 'seed of beast.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If he read Torah but did not learn משנה, he is a בור. If he did neither, the פסוק says about him: 'I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man and the seed of beast.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the previous step keeps going and adds two lower levels below the עם הארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds a ladder. Someone who learned but did not serve תלמידי חכמים is an עם הארץ. Someone who learned only מקרא is a בור. Someone who learned nothing at all is compared to an animal. Each level shows less Torah than the one before it.

keyTerms.meaning: Read, meaning studied the written Torah (מקרא)
Learned משנה, the oral teachings
A boor, a person with no real learning
Seed of beast; here it describes someone with no Torah at all

phrases.aramaic: קָרָא וְלֹא שָׁנָה — הֲרֵי זֶה בּוּר,
phrases.english: If he read but did not learn — he is a boor,
if he did not read and did not learn —
about him the verse says:
"And I will sow the house of Israel
and the house of Judah
with the seed of man and the seed of beast."

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרָא וְלֹא שָׁנָה — הֲרֵי זֶה בּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with lower levels of ignorance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading without learning משנה makes one a בור. Learning nothing at all is compared to an animal.

steps.title: רבי יצחק explains 'those who repeat' as people who repeat הלכות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק reads 'שונים' in a פסוק in משלי as people who repeat הלכות by rote, and says one should not mix with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'My son, fear the Lord and the king, and do not mix with those who repeat.' רבי יצחק said: these are people who repeat הלכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new פסוק, and רבי יצחק explains who the 'שונים' in it are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the theme of learning without understanding. The 'שונים' are people who repeat הלכות by memory but do not know the reasons behind them.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who repeat; here, people who recite הלכות
Do not mix in, do not get involved
Laws, rulings

phrases.english: "My son, fear the Lord and the king,
and do not mix with those who repeat."
Rabbi Yitzchak said:
These are those who repeat halachot.
phrases.notes: He means people who keep repeating the laws but don't understand the reasons behind them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: אֵלּוּ שֶׁשּׁוֹנִים הֲלָכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new פסוק on a related theme: learning without proper understanding.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'שונים' one should avoid are people who repeat הלכות without understanding them.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יצחק needed to say this at all, since the meaning seems plain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק: what new idea is he teaching? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'שונים' naturally means 'those who repeat learning.' So the גמרא wants to know what other reading רבי יצחק is ruling out.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; why say it?

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבי יצחק's statement adds anything new.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the meaning is plain, there is no need to state it.

steps.title: We might have thought it means repeating sins, as רב הונא teaches
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'שונים' could have been read as people who repeat sins, based on רב הונא's teaching. רבי יצחק teaches that this is not the meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said it means people who repeat a sin, as רב הונא says: once a person sins and repeats it, it becomes permitted to him. So רבי יצחק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows another possible reading of the פסוק that רבי יצחק is ruling out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא teaches that repeating a sin makes it feel permitted. So the פסוק could have been warning against people who repeat sins. רבי יצחק tells us the פסוק is really about people who repeat הלכות by rote.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said
Repeated it, did the sin a second time
It became permitted to him (in his own eyes)
This teaches us

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא does not mean the sin truly becomes permitted. He means the sinner starts to feel that it is allowed.

phrases.english: You might have said
that it means those who repeat in sin,
in line with Rav Huna.
For Rav Huna said:
once a person commits a sin
and repeats it — it becomes permitted to him,
phrases.notes: Permitted in his own eyes, because he has gotten used to it.

phrases.english: so he teaches us.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'פשיטא' challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing another possible reading that the statement rules out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק might refer to people who repeat sins, following רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק refers to people who repeat הלכות by rote.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the תנאים wear down the world
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that the תנאים, people who memorize and recite teachings, are 'מבלי עולם,' people who wear down the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: the תנאים wear down the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a surprising ברייתא about the people who recite Torah teachings from memory.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'תנאים' does not mean the great Sages of the משנה. It means the people whose job was to memorize and recite teachings. The harsh label sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
Here, people who memorize and recite teachings
Those who wear down or destroy the world

steps.confusionAlert: 'תנאים' here does not mean the Sages of the משנה. It means the reciters who memorized texts.

phrases.english: It was taught:
The tanna'im wear down the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: הַתַּנָּאִים — מְבַלֵּי עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of learning by rote, now with a sharper statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The reciting תנאים are called מבלי עולם.

steps.title: Could they really wear down the world?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is amazed: how can people who learn Torah be called destroyers of the world?
steps.simpleTranslation: Could you really think they wear down the world?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא, since people who learn Torah should be building the world. This sets up רבינא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Torah study is supposed to hold up the world. So calling Torah learners 'מבלי עולם' seems impossible as stated.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind?

phrases.english: Could it enter your mind that they wear down the world?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מְבַלֵּי עוֹלָם סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא calling the תנאים מבלי עולם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: People who learn Torah build the world. They cannot be destroying it.

steps.title: רבינא: they rule הלכה straight from their משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that the ברייתא means those who give halachic rulings directly from the משנה they memorized, without knowing the reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: it means those who rule הלכה from their memorized משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the challenge by narrowing whom the ברייתא is criticizing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Learning itself is not the problem. The harm comes from giving rulings based only on the wording of a משנה, without understanding the reasons and the later discussion. Rulings like that can be wrong, and that is what damages the world.

keyTerms.meaning: Give halachic rulings
From their memorized משנה

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Those who rule halacha from their Mishnah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: שֶׁמּוֹרִין הֲלָכָה מִתּוֹךְ מִשְׁנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All reciters of teachings are being criticized.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only those who rule הלכה from the bare wording of the משנה are מבלי עולם.

steps.title: A ברייתא of רבי יהושע supports רבינא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that רבי יהושע asked the same question, proved from a פסוק that Torah learners settle the world, and gave רבינא's same answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this. רבי יהושע said: do they wear down the world? Don't they settle the world, as it says 'His ways are eternal'? Rather, it means those who rule הלכה from their משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רבינא said, which supports his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע reads 'הליכות' as 'הלכות,' so the פסוק shows that people who learn הלכות hold up the world. That is why he too concludes that only those who rule from the משנה without understanding are criticized. This matches רבינא.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this
Those who settle, build up the world
Eternal ways; read here as 'הלכות'

steps.whatToRemember: Learning הלכות builds the world. Giving rulings from memorized משניות without understanding them damages it.

phrases.english: It was also taught so:
Rabbi Yehoshua said:
Do they wear down the world?
Don't they settle the world,
as it says: "His ways are eternal"!
Rather, it means those who rule halacha from their Mishnah.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבינא's answer with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי יהושע and חבקוק 3:6

steps.title: Back to the משנה: more people who wear down the world
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's 'אשה פרושה' and quotes a ברייתא listing a constantly praying maiden, a widow who keeps visiting neighbors, and a baby born early as 'מבלי עולם.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says 'an abstinent woman' and so on. The רבנן taught: a maiden who keeps praying, a widow who keeps going around to neighbors, and a baby whose months were not completed. These wear down the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the next phrase in the משנה and brings a ברייתא with more examples of 'מבלי עולם.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed an 'אשה פרושה' among those who wear down the world. The ברייתא adds similar cases where extreme or unusual behavior, or an early birth, is counted in the same category.

keyTerms.meaning: An abstinent, overly separated woman
A maiden who prays all the time
A widow who keeps going around to neighbors
His months (of pregnancy) were not completed

phrases.english: "An abstinent woman," etc.
The Rabbis taught:
a maiden who prays constantly,
and a widow who goes around to neighbors,
and a baby whose months were not completed —
these wear down the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִשָּׁה פְּרוּשָׁה וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's list after finishing the discussion of the תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A constantly praying maiden, a widow who keeps visiting neighbors, and a baby born before term are counted as מבלי עולם.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי יוחנן learned good things from a maiden and a widow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the ברייתא's criticism of the praying maiden and the widow, using רבי יוחנן's statement that he learned fear of sin from a maiden and receiving reward from a widow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really true? But רבי יוחנן said: We learned fear of sin from a maiden, and receiving reward from a widow!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the ברייתא from step 15, which said a praying maiden and a visiting widow wear down the world. It brings רבי יוחנן, who learned positive lessons from exactly these kinds of women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treated a constantly praying maiden and a widow who goes out a lot as harmful. רבי יוחנן says he learned important lessons from a maiden and a widow. So how can such women be criticized? The next two steps tell the stories behind his statement.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? This word opens a challenge.
Fear of sin, being careful not to do wrong
Receiving reward for a מצוה
A maiden, an unmarried young woman

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
We learned fear of sin from a maiden,
and receiving reward from a widow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא quoted in step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא calling a praying maiden and a visiting widow 'מבלי עולם'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן learned praiseworthy lessons from a maiden and a widow, so such women cannot simply be called destroyers of the world.

steps.title: The maiden who prayed not to cause others to sin
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן heard a maiden pray that no man should stumble into sin because of her. That is where he learned fear of sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fear of sin from a maiden: רבי יוחנן heard a certain maiden fall on her face and say: Master of the world, You created גן עדן and You created גיהנם, You created righteous people and You created wicked people. May it be Your will that people not stumble because of me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half of רבי יוחנן's statement by telling the story of the maiden he heard praying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her prayer shows real fear of sin. She was not only worried about her own sins. She also worried that others might sin because of her and end up in גיהנם. This makes the challenge stronger, because her constant prayer was clearly a good thing.

keyTerms.meaning: She fell on her face, meaning she prayed with deep humility
Paradise, the place of reward
The place of punishment
They will stumble, meaning come to sin

phrases.english: Fear of sin from a maiden:
for Rabbi Yochanan heard a certain maiden
who fell on her face and was saying:
Master of the world,
You created Gan Eden and You created Gehinnom,
You created righteous people and You created wicked people.
May it be Your will
that people should not stumble because of me.

steps.triggerLanguage: יִרְאַת חֵטְא מִבְּתוּלָה — דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן שַׁמְעַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the story behind the first half of רבי יוחנן's statement
steps.raayaObject: That a praying maiden can be praiseworthy
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's experience hearing a maiden's prayer

steps.title: The widow who walked far to pray for the reward of her steps
steps.stepSummary: A widow passed by the shul in her own neighborhood to pray in רבי יוחנן's בית מדרש every day, because she wanted the reward for her steps.
steps.simpleTranslation: Receiving reward from a widow: there was a certain widow who had a shul in her neighborhood. Every day she came and prayed in רבי יוחנן's בית מדרש. He said to her: My daughter, isn't there a shul in your neighborhood? She said to him: רבי, don't I get reward for the steps?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second half of רבי יוחנן's statement with the story of a widow who walked far to pray.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The widow left her house every day and walked a long way, which looks like the 'going around' the ברייתא criticized. Yet רבי יוחנן learned from her that every step taken for a מצוה earns reward. This completes the challenge from both women.

keyTerms.meaning: A synagogue (Aramaic for בית הכנסת)
Neighborhood
Study hall
Reward for the steps walked to do a מצוה

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן learned two lessons: fear of sin from a maiden's prayer, and the reward for every step taken toward a מצוה from a widow.

phrases.english: Receiving reward from a widow:
for there was a certain widow
who had a synagogue in her neighborhood.
Every day she would come
and pray in the study hall of Rabbi Yochanan.
He said to her: My daughter,
isn't there a synagogue in your neighborhood?
She said to him: Rabbi,
don't I get reward for the steps?

steps.triggerLanguage: קִיבּוּל שָׂכָר מֵאַלְמָנָה — דְּהָהִיא אַלְמָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the story behind the second half of רבי יוחנן's statement
steps.raayaObject: That a widow who goes out often can be praiseworthy
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's conversation with the widow who prayed in his בית מדרש

steps.title: The ברייתא means someone like יוחני בת רטיבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is not criticizing truly pious women. It means someone like יוחני בת רטיבי, who only looked pious.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the ברייתא said it, it meant someone like יוחני בת רטיבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It narrows the ברייתא so that it only speaks about a fake kind of piety.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The women in רבי יוחנן's stories were truly G-d-fearing, so they really are praiseworthy. The ברייתא speaks about someone like יוחני בת רטיבי. She made a show of constant prayer but actually practiced sorcery. Both sources can now be true: real piety is praised, and fake piety harms the world.

keyTerms.meaning: When it says, meaning what the source actually refers to
For example, someone like
A woman known for looking pious while actually doing sorcery

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's 'מבלי עולם' is about fake piety, like יוחני בת רטיבי. Sincere prayer and walking far for a מצוה are praised.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that praying a lot or going to pray is bad. It is only criticizing people who use a show of piety to cover up wrongdoing.

phrases.english: When it says it,
phrases.notes: This means: when the ברייתא calls the praying woman 'מבלי עולם'.

phrases.english: it means someone like Yochani bat Retivi.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָאָמַר, כְּגוֹן יוֹחָנִי בַּת רְטִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in steps 16-18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the ברייתא refers only to fake piety
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא condemns any woman who prays constantly or goes out a lot, which would contradict רבי יוחנן
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא refers to hypocrites like יוחני בת רטיבי, while sincere women are praised

steps.title: What is 'a baby whose months were not complete'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means by the third item on its list: a baby born before its months were complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'a baby whose months were not completed'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the last item on the ברייתא's list from step 15 and asks what it means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A baby born early has done nothing wrong, so it is strange to call it 'מבלי עולם'. The גמרא asks for the real meaning of this phrase.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby whose months of pregnancy were not completed, born too early
What is the meaning of

phrases.english: What is meant by 'a baby whose months were not completed'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״קָטָן שֶׁלֹּא כָּלוּ לוֹ חֳדָשָׁיו״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא of step 15 to explain its third item
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'a baby whose months were not complete' in the list of מבלי עולם

steps.title: It means a תלמיד חכם who scorns his teachers
steps.stepSummary: In בבל they explained that the 'premature baby' is a תלמיד חכם who scorns his teachers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here in בבל they explained: this is a תלמיד חכם who scorns his teachers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by reading the phrase as a picture of a certain kind of person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A baby born before it is fully formed is a picture of a student who is not yet fully 'formed' in his learning. Even so, he acts as if he no longer needs his teachers and looks down on them. A student like that is the one the ברייתא calls מבלי עולם.

keyTerms.meaning: Here (in בבל) they explained it
A Torah scholar
Who kicks at, meaning scorns, his teachers

steps.whatToRemember: The 'premature baby' in the ברייתא is not a real baby. It is a picture of an unfinished תלמיד חכם who scorns his teachers.

phrases.english: Here they explained it:
phrases.notes: 'Here' means in בבל, where this גמרא was learned.

phrases.english: this is a Torah scholar who scorns his teachers.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא תַּרְגִּימוּ: זֶה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם הַמְבַעֵט בְּרַבּוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The premature baby is a picture of an unfinished תלמיד חכם who scorns his teachers

steps.title: רבי אבא: A student who rules before he is ready
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא explains the 'premature baby' as a student who has not yet reached the level of הוראה but still issues rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא says: The 'premature baby' is a student who has not yet reached the level of giving rulings, and yet he gives rulings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the question from step 20: who is the 'baby born before its months were complete'? רבי אבא says it is a student who rules on הלכה too early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The picture fits well. A premature baby comes out before it is fully formed, and this student 'comes out' as a פוסק before he is fully ready. This is a different answer from the one given in בבל (a scholar who scorns his teachers).

keyTerms.meaning: A student, someone still learning
Reached the level of being able to issue rulings
Issues a halachic ruling

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba says:
This is a student who has not reached the level of issuing rulings
phrases.notes: 'This' means the 'baby born before its months were complete' from the ברייתא's list.

phrases.english: and yet he issues rulings.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר: זֶה תַּלְמִיד שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ לְהוֹרָאָה וּמוֹרֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative explanation to the בבל answer in step 21 for the same question in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is meant by 'a baby born before its months were complete'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A student who has not reached the level of הוראה but issues rulings anyway.

steps.title: רב's teaching: 'She has cast down many wounded' is the student who rules too early
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רבי אבא with רב's דרשה: 'כי רבים חללים הפילה' refers to a תלמיד חכם who rules before he is ready.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אבהו said in the name of רב הונא in the name of רב: What does the פסוק mean, 'For she has cast down many wounded, and mighty are all her slain'? 'For she has cast down many wounded': this is a תלמיד חכם who has not reached the level of ruling, and yet he rules.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to back up רבי אבא. רב reads the first half of a פסוק in משלי as talking about a scholar who rules too early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works through the word הִפִּילָה ('cast down'), which shares a root with נֵפֶל, a baby born before its time. So the פסוק itself links 'premature' language to a scholar who rules before he is ready. It also shows how harmful this is: such rulings 'cast down many wounded.'

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written: a standard way to open the explanation of a פסוק
Wounded or fallen people
She cast down, made fall
A Torah scholar

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for the danger of issuing halachic rulings before one is qualified.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Abahu said
that Rav Huna said that Rav said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"For she has cast down many wounded,
and mighty are all her slain"?
"For she has cast down many wounded":
phrases.notes: הִפִּילָה sounds like נֵפֶל, a baby born too early. That is the link to רבי אבא's 'premature baby.'

phrases.english: this is a Torah scholar
who has not reached the level of issuing rulings, and yet he issues rulings.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides support from a פסוק for רבי אבא's explanation in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבא's claim that the 'premature' one is a student who rules too early.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's דרשה on משלי 7:26, 'כי רבים חללים הפילה.'

steps.title: The second half: a qualified scholar who refuses to rule
steps.stepSummary: רב reads 'ועצומים כל הרוגיה' as a qualified תלמיד חכם who does not issue rulings, which is also harmful.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And mighty are all her slain': this is a תלמיד חכם who has reached the level of ruling, and does not rule.
steps.whatsHappening: רב finishes his explanation of the פסוק with its second half. It warns about the opposite mistake: a scholar who is qualified but holds back from ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half condemned ruling too early. The second half says that refusing to rule when you are qualified also 'kills,' and the victims are 'many and mighty.' Both extremes cause harm. This half is not needed for רבי אבא's proof; it completes רב's teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Mighty or numerous
Her slain ones
And he does not issue rulings

steps.whatToRemember: רב's פסוק teaches both sides. Ruling before you are ready causes harm, and refusing to rule when you are ready also causes harm.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the second half proves רבי אבא's point. Only the first half (הִפִּילָה) connects to the 'premature baby.' The second half is the rest of רב's teaching.

phrases.english: "And mighty are all her slain":
this is a Torah scholar
who has reached the level of issuing rulings, and does not issue rulings.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַעֲצוּמִים כׇּל הֲרוּגֶיהָ — זֶה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְהוֹרָאָה וְאֵינוֹ מוֹרֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב's דרשה from step 23 by explaining the second half of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A qualified תלמיד חכם who refuses to issue rulings causes great harm, like 'mighty slain.'
